response: Yes, it may be time to reconsider lobectomy in low-risk pediatric thyroid cancer. According to recent findings, ultrasound and histopathology can identify a substantial population of low-risk patients who may be candidates for lobectomy, avoiding the risks and potential medical and psychosocial morbidity associated with total thyroidectomy. A proposed clinical framework suggests that lobectomy could be a viable option for these patients, and it is worth discussing and considering this approach to provide the best possible care for low-risk pediatric thyroid cancer patients.
